AssetReference.description: Reference to a visual asset with semantic type classification. Enables rich visual associations for practice elements.

assetName.description: Name of an Asset in the same aggregate (symbolic link; must match Asset.name in top-level assets array).

type.description: Semantic type of asset usage. icon: UI markers, visual identity (e.g., alpha icons, competency badges). illustrative: Documentation diagrams, architecture visualizations, workflow charts. template: Reusable documents, forms, decision records. diagram: Technical architecture, state progression, pattern orchestration.

PracticeElement.description: Common identity and prose fields for named practice artifacts. tags optional: omit, structured buckets, or legacy string[].

tags.description: Canonical shape: orthogonal tag buckets. Legacy interchange: flat string array (tooling treats it as lifecycleTags only).

oneOf.description: Deprecated interchange; prefer the structured object.

narratives.description: Optional narrative breakdown embedded on any practice element (language.mmd).

assetNames.description: Optional array of asset references with semantic type classification (0..*). Enables multiple visual associations per element (e.g., alpha with both icon and state diagram).

contributingPatternName.description: Name of the Pattern that contributed this element during merge. Set by the merge algorithm to record pattern-level provenance — which pattern introduced or enriched this element. Complements sourcePracticeName (practice-level provenance) with finer-grained pattern-level attribution. Do not set in source practice authoring; populated automatically during composition.

specificityName.description: The dimension of specificity this practice's redeclaration adds to the element — redeclaration makes an element more specific rather than narrowing its scope. Valid only on a redeclaration of an element inherited through the dependency tree; an error on a net-new element or a document root.

specificity.description: Merge-populated. The accumulated specificity chain for this element across the practices actually loaded, most specific first. Recomputed per composition, never authored — declaring it in a source document is a validation error.

suppressed.description: When true, this inherited element is switched off in the composed result, letting a restricted variant diminish what it inherits rather than only adding to it. Valid only on an element inherited through the baseline chain or a practice dependency. Because every element and part type extends PracticeElement, one property reaches whole elements (alphas, work products, activities, patterns) and parts of elements (states, levels of detail, checklist items) alike. Where another loaded document still requires a suppressed element, the conflict resolves by declaration precedence — see semantics/composition.md section 4.9.

NarrativeContext.description: One slice of authored narrative keyed to a narrative element (STRING ref; resolve to NarrativeElement.name on the parent NarrativeType).

narrativeElementName.description: Symbolic link to NarrativeElement.name inside the NarrativeType named by enclosing Narrative.narrativeTypeName.

howToUse.description: Guidance for applying this spine element.

narrativeElements.description: Embedded narrative spine elements owned by this type (composition; language.mmd).

narrativeTypeName.description: Symbolic link to NarrativeType.name in scope (baseline narrativeTypes or practice overlay).

citationNames.description: Optional array of Citation.name references (symbolic links to citations in the same practice/method scope).

authors.description: The person, group, or organization responsible for the work (e.g., ['Skelton, M.', 'Pais, M.']).

source.description: Publisher, journal, or URL where the work can be retrieved.

url.description: URL or DOI where the work can be retrieved.

pages.description: Page range or location within the cited work, following APA 7th edition format. For journal articles: 'pp. 112-127'. For book chapters: 'pp. 45-67'. For specific references: 'p. 23'. For online works without pages: 'para. 4' or 'Section 2.1'.

url.description: Optional URL associated with the acknowledgement, for example contact email `mailto:xx` or hyperlink to a profile page

description.description: Human-readable description of what the asset depicts and its purpose

path.description: Relative path to the asset file (e.g., 'assets/diagrams/pattern-lifecycle.svg')

dataUri.description: Optional base64-encoded data URI for small assets (<10KB)

url.description: Optional external URL for remotely-hosted assets

fontFamily.description: Font family name for font-character assets (e.g., 'Font Awesome 6 Free', 'Material Icons')

fontUrl.description: Optional URL to load the font from (e.g., Google Fonts, Font Awesome CDN, custom font file). If not provided, assumes font is already available.

ExternalLink.description: A reference to an external document or resource associated with an instance. Captures the name and purpose of the linked content, with an optional URI when the resource has a stable address.

name.description: Short label identifying the linked resource (e.g., 'Sprint Backlog', 'Architecture Decision Record').

description.description: Explanation of what this resource contains or why it is linked.

uri.description: URI of the external resource, when available. Accepts absolute URLs (e.g. an RHSC record) or relative references (e.g. a markdown file beside the Project JSON).

pages.description: Page or location reference within the linked resource, following APA 7th edition format. Examples: 'p. 5' (single page), 'pp. 12-15' (page range), 'Chapter 3', 'Section 2.1', 'para. 4', 'Table 2'. Use when the relevant content is at a specific location within a larger document.

kind.description: Optional classification of the linked resource type. Tool-agnostic: describes what the resource IS, not which tool hosts it. When absent, the link is unclassified.

Note.description: Timestamped commentary for project tracking. Notes are intended to be brief summaries; use the links array to reference longer documents such as meeting transcripts or detailed reports. Appears at multiple levels within a Project (top-level, plan, current, target, team, checklist states).

name.description: Short summary or title of the note.

timestamp.description: ISO timestamp string recording when the note was created.

content.description: The note text. Keep brief — use links for detailed supporting material.

links.description: Optional array of external resource references providing supporting detail (e.g., meeting transcripts, design documents, external reports).
